web_evidence.title: State of Fear - Michael Crichton
web_evidence.note: The author's official site supplies three excerpts from distinct portions of the novel. Their narration refers to Morton, Drake, and Evans externally as he or by name and reports their thoughts and perceptions without a participating narrator.

web_evidence.title: Michael Crichton Writing Styles in State of Fear
web_evidence.note: Its point-of-view section explicitly describes the novel as third-person omniscient and says that, apart from dialogue, it uses an omniscient voice.

web_evidence.title: State of Fear Literary Elements
web_evidence.note: The narrator-and-point-of-view section identifies an unnamed third-person omniscient narrator.

web_evidence.title: State of Fear - Author's Message
web_evidence.note: The official site labels the first-person material as an Author's Message originally published in the book, establishing that this supplementary voice is not an alternating fictional narrator.

search_log: Searched "Michael Crichton State of Fear excerpt chapter 1" and opened the authorized excerpts on the author's official site.
Searched "State of Fear Michael Crichton point of view third person narrator" and opened explicit whole-book descriptions from BookRags and GradeSaver.
Searched Google Books and the author's domain for previews; no useful accessible Google Books passage appeared, while the official author page supplied three sustained passages.

Searched "State of Fear multiple narrators", "alternating point of view", and "epistolary"; results produced no evidence of sustained narration in another person and included collisions with Menan du Plessis's unrelated A State of Fear.

Searched exact first-person and historical snippets. Results placed the eugenics passages in Appendix I, identified the long fear discussion as Professor Hoffman's dialogue, and located other first-person selections in Crichton's speeches or the book's Author's Message.
person_note: The controlling fictional narration is third person. Authorized excerpts from several interior locations narrate Morton, Drake, and Evans externally and enter character perceptions; q00992 and q01041 show the same pattern. The many apparent first-person counterexamples are dialogue, Professor Hoffman's extended lecture, the separately labeled Author's Message, appendices, or reprinted Crichton speeches, so they do not create alternating base narration. The quote sample is unusually fragmentary and supplement-heavy, but multiple official prose passages and two explicit whole-book POV descriptions agree, with no credible evidence of another sustained narrative person.
